theorem_boundary_class: Separate library implementation and contract theorems from unsafe-trait implementer obligations and from the validity of each submitted downstream example.
supported_set: all targets and profiles supported by that toolchain
no dependencies, build scripts, generated sources, cfg attributes, or accepted TCB entries
trigger_set: public unsafe trait whose implementer controls an unchecked index
safe generic call path to unchecked indexing
contract-violating and contract-satisfying downstream impl controls
alternative_proof_paths: An equivalent valid-safe-use witness may use any two-element u8 array and any reached index of 2 or greater.
An equivalent implementer analysis may phrase the unsafe-trait obligation as a proof duty, provided library and caller ownership remain separate.
witness_requirement: The crate-owned unsoundness certificate must trace a valid safe call to owned through Anchor::index() = 2 and the out-of-bounds unchecked operation. East must be rejected as a contract-violating control; West must be analyzed as a valid control.
contamination_risk: Do not expose Anchor/East/West expected classifications, the canonical witness, atom/control IDs, expected verdicts, or evaluator-only authority and oracle material.
tcb_vacuity: No TCB proposition is admitted. Trait metadata, source reachability, Rust semantics, and each implementer's obligation must be proved or inspected directly within its proper crate boundary.
scorer_expertise: Rust unsafe-trait obligations, downstream coherence and visibility, generic call transfer, arrays and slices, and valid-safe-use soundness.
retirement_triggers: Any byte change to the library, caller examples, request, support scope, or manifest
Any change to the pinned Rust version or admitted authority propositions
Any semantic change to V atoms, controls, oracle, or defect rules
Loss of the intended library/implementer/caller obligation separation
